title: Four Bins at the Gate: What Really Happens to a Sorted Bag
title_zh: 门口的四只桶：一只分好类的垃圾袋究竟去了哪里
intro_zh: 本文约 532 词，以城市小区垃圾投放点为切入点，讲清厨余垃圾、可回收物与有害垃圾分别会被怎样处理，并给出具体数据，说明“前端分类”与“后端处理”必须彼此配合，才能真正把垃圾变成资源。全文含 6 个 CET-4 核心词，句子难度中等。

paragraphs.en: At seven in the morning, the bin station at the gate of a Shanghai neighbourhood is busy. People arrive with two or three bags and drop them into four coloured containers: dark grey for kitchen waste, blue for recyclables, red for hazardous items, black for everything else. A volunteer in an orange vest lifts one lid, looks inside, and says, 'This bag is fine.'
paragraphs.zh: 早上七点，上海某小区门口的垃圾投放点一派忙碌。人们拎着两三个袋子走来，把它们分别丢进四只不同颜色的桶里：深灰色装厨余垃圾，蓝色装可回收物，红色装有害垃圾，黑色装其余垃圾。一位穿橙色马甲的志愿者掀开一只桶盖，往里看了一眼，说：“这袋没问题。”

paragraphs.en: A single bag of mixed rubbish is hard to deal with. Leftover rice and wet vegetable leaves carry a lot of water. When they are thrown in with paper and cardboard, the paper turns soft and useless, and the whole truckload may end up buried or burned. Sorting, in the end, is the cheapest way to keep clean materials clean.
paragraphs.zh: 一袋混装的垃圾很难处理。剩饭和湿菜叶带着大量水分，一旦和纸张、纸板丢在一起，纸就会变软、变得毫无用处，整车的垃圾最后可能只能被填埋或焚烧。说到底，分类是让干净的材料保持干净的最省钱的办法。

paragraphs.en: Chinese cities produce more than 200 million tonnes of household rubbish a year, and about half of it is kitchen waste. That is a problem and also a resource. At a treatment plant, the scraps are heated and then eaten by bacteria inside huge closed tanks. The process of letting them digest takes about three weeks, and it gives off a gas that can be converted into electricity for the city grid.
paragraphs.zh: 中国的城市每年产生两亿多吨生活垃圾，其中大约一半是厨余垃圾。这既是麻烦，也是资源。在处理厂里，这些剩菜剩饭先被加热，再在巨大的密闭罐中被细菌“吃掉”。让它们消化的过程大约需要三周，过程中会释放出一种气体，可以转化成电力输入城市电网。

paragraphs.en: The numbers are surprising. One tonne of kitchen waste can yield about 100 cubic metres of gas, enough to cook meals for a family for several months. What is left at the end is a dark, dry material that farmers use to feed the soil, so nothing has to go to a landfill. In a city of ten million people, all this adds up to a quiet power station that nobody ever has to see.
paragraphs.zh: 数据出人意料。一吨厨余垃圾大约能产出 100 立方米气体，足够一家人做几个月的饭。最后剩下的是一种深色干燥的物质，农民用它来肥田，因此没有任何东西需要进垃圾填埋场。在一座千万人口的城市里，这些加起来就是一座安静运转、谁都不必看见的发电站。

paragraphs.en: Recyclables carry real value. Recycling one tonne of paper saves about seventeen trees and half of the water needed to make new paper. Aluminium is even better: a can made from old cans uses only five percent of the energy. But that value disappears when materials are contaminated. A greasy pizza box or a bottle still half full of milk can spoil a whole bale of paper or plastic, and the bale is then burned.
paragraphs.zh: 可回收物是真正有价值的。回收一吨纸，可以少砍约十七棵树，并省下生产新纸所需的一半用水。铝更划算：用旧易拉罐做成的罐子只用掉百分之五的能源。但一旦材料被污染，这些价值就消失了。一只沾满油渍的披萨盒，或一只还剩半瓶牛奶的瓶子，就能毁掉整捆纸或塑料，而这捆东西随后只能被烧掉。

paragraphs.en: Hazardous waste is a small pile with a long shadow. Old batteries, broken thermometers and expired medicines together make up less than one percent of what households throw out, yet they must never be disposed of like ordinary rubbish. A single button battery, once its case breaks, can contaminate 600,000 litres of water — more than one person could drink in a lifetime.
paragraphs.zh: 有害垃圾是一小堆、长影子：分量轻，危害却长久。旧电池、碎温度计和过期药品加起来不到家庭丢弃物的百分之一，但它们绝不能被当作普通垃圾处理。一颗纽扣电池的外壳一旦破损，就能污染 60 万升水——比一个人一辈子喝的水还多。

paragraphs.en: Good systems make the right choice easy. Cities that place the bins close to the door, print clear pictures on the lids and keep the station clean get far better results than cities that only hand out rules. In some communities, families scan a card when they drop off their recyclables and collect points for small rewards — an efficient reminder rather than a lecture.
paragraphs.zh: 好的制度会让正确的选择变得容易。把垃圾桶设在离楼门很近的地方、在桶盖上印清楚图案、让投放点保持干净，这样的城市成效远好于那些只发规定的城市。在一些社区，家庭投放可回收物时刷卡积分，可以换取小奖励——这是高效的提醒，而不是说教。

paragraphs.en: None of this works in one direction only. A truck cannot sort what a household has already crushed together, and a household will stop sorting if the bins are never emptied. Waste is not really thrown away at all — it simply moves somewhere else. Every well-sorted bag is a short message to the city, and the city, slowly, is learning to read it.
paragraphs.zh: 这一切都不是单向奏效的。一辆清运车无法分拣一个家庭已经混在一起压紧的垃圾；而如果桶里的垃圾从来没人清运，家庭也会不再分类。垃圾其实从来没有被真正“扔掉”，它只是挪到了别的地方。每一只认真分好类的袋子，都是写给这座城市的一条短消息，而城市正在慢慢学会读懂它。

questions.q: Why does the passage mention a greasy pizza box and a bottle half full of milk?
options: They are too heavy for the collection truck to lift.
They can ruin a whole bale of recyclable material.
They make the bin station smell unpleasant in summer.
They have to be sent to a special medical plant.
questions.explain: 细节题。第五段明确指出，沾油的披萨盒或剩半瓶牛奶的瓶子会“毁掉整捆纸或塑料”，使其只能被焚烧，因此选第二项。

questions.q: What happens to kitchen waste at a treatment plant?
options: It is dried and then buried in a landfill.
It is burned to heat the closed tanks.
Bacteria break it down and produce gas for electricity.
It is sold to farmers exactly as it arrives.
questions.explain: 细节题。第三段说明厨余垃圾被加热后由密闭罐中的细菌消化，约三周后释放出可转化为电力的气体；第四段补充残渣才被农民用来肥田，故第三项正确。

questions.q: The phrase 'a small pile with a long shadow' suggests that hazardous waste ____.
options: takes up most of the space in the black bin
is collected less often than other kinds of waste
weighs more than ordinary household rubbish
is small in amount but can cause lasting harm
questions.explain: 词义/句意理解题。该比喻后紧跟数据：有害垃圾不到家庭垃圾的百分之一，但一颗纽扣电池可污染 60 万升水，说明“量小危害久”，故选第四项。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Sorting rubbish is mainly a moral duty that individuals must carry alone.
Modern machines can separate mixed waste without any human help.
Household sorting and city services must work together to turn waste into resources.
Kitchen waste is the only kind of rubbish that is worth sorting.
questions.explain: 主旨题。全文分别讲厨余、可回收物、有害垃圾的去向，末段强调“分类不是单向的”：家庭与清运、处理系统必须彼此配合，故第三项最能概括全文。
